Alex / Lisa — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we captured so we can get a formal pricing proposal out: 

1) Volume profile (please confirm numbers in the attached spreadsheet):
   - Expected steady-state monthly tokens: 45M–60M (Apogee indicated mid-point ~52M)
   - Expected launch month spike: +20–30% initial surge
   - 99th-percentile peak TPS observed in demo: ~280 TPS average for the simulated load; you mentioned potential flash events up to ~320 TPS (99th).

2) Budget / unit target you mentioned on the call: $12–$16 per 1M tokens as a target range for a committed plan.

3) Key commercial asks:
   - Do you need a 12-month committed slab vs month-to-month?
   - Any procurement/PO cadence or doc templates we should plan for (PO, SOW, vendor form)?

Next steps I propose: I’ll draft a short hosted pricing proposal and call out committed vs on-demand lanes, burst windows, and SLA/99th latency expectations. Can you confirm the numbers in the attached Apogee_Monthly_Traffic_Estimate.xlsx (especially the 99th TPS column)? Once we have that, I’ll circulate a pricing PDF and propose a 30-min procurement intro with Karthik (cc’d) to walk PO/SOW and discount mechanics.

Attachments: Apogee_Monthly_Traffic_Estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet — traffic projection per month, week-of-day TPS columns)

Thanks,
Hannah

Thanks, Hannah — short answers from our side after reviewing the internal traffic estimates: 

- Confirmed steady-state monthly tokens: 52,000,000 (we expect variation +/-10% depending on marketing pushes).
- Launch month: could hit ~70M if our campaign performs; typical ramp in first 6–8 weeks.
- Peak (99th) TPS: our infra team measured historical event patterns and we’re comfortable planning for sustained 280–320 TPS peaks, with very short bursts to ~420 TPS for handful of minutes during heavy events.

Budget: we’re aiming for a committed price in the $14/1M range, but will need to see a structured slab to evaluate. Can you show a 12-month committed tier and a 24-month option? Also want clarity on how burst over-commit is billed (do bursts pull from committed volume or billed overage at on-demand price?). 

Procurement: looping in Lisa (cc) who owns vendor onboarding and contract terms — Lisa, happy to coordinate a short call to go over vendor docs and any security checklist items.

Appreciate a quick sample invoice cadence and whether Redwood supports monthly invoicing against a committed prepay or net-30 invoicing.

Cheers,
Alex Mercer
Head of Product, Apogee Health
alex.mercer@apogeehealth.io
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Apogee hosted API: monthly token forecast + peak TPS (post-demo recap)

Alex / Lisa — thanks for the confirmation and the spike guidance. I put together an initial hosted pricing proposal (attached) that addresses committed slabs, burst behavior, and invoice cadence. High-level summary here so you can scan quickly: 

1) Pricing lanes (illustrative, final after traffic file reconfirmation):
   - On-demand (no commit): $20 / 1M tokens
   - 12-month commit tiers:
       * 30M committed: $16 / 1M
       * 45M committed: $14 / 1M
       * 60M+ committed: $12 / 1M
   - 24-month commit: additional 5–10% off the 12-month tier (subject to SLA and payment terms)

2) Burst policy and billing mechanics:
   - Short bursts (<=5 minutes) are tolerated and do not count against committed volume if they remain within a configured burst window.
   - Sustained usage above committed monthly allowance is billed as overage at the on-demand rate, unless a temporary burst credit is purchased in advance. We can include automatic burst protection for the first 2 weeks post-launch.

3) Invoice / payment options:
   - Monthly invoicing (net-30) against committed slabs is supported.
   - Prepay discounts available for annual upfront payment.

4) SLA / ops notes:
   - SLOs for 99th latency and availability will be called out in the SOW. We support canary rollouts and fallback routing to smaller model variants to preserve availability during infrastructure pressure.

Attachments: Redwood_hosted-pricing-proposal.pdf (sample slab table, burst rules, SLA bullets)

Proposed next steps (pick one):
   • 30-min procurement + billing intro (Karthik + Lisa) to confirm PO/SOW details and invoice cadence — suggest Thu 26 Aug 15:00–15:30 UTC or Fri 27 Aug 14:00–14:30 UTC.
   • Finalize traffic workbook (attached) — Alex, if you can mark the expected monthly column and highlight any months you expect marketing-driven spikes, that will let me produce a final price illustration.

If that sounds good I’ll lock the meeting and share a short one-pager for Lisa to use in vendor onboarding.

Best,
Hannah
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
